qr_code_generator.name: QR Code Generator
qr_code_generator.description: Generate QR codes from text, URLs, or any data instantly.

seo.intro: This free QR code generator online lets you create custom QR codes from any text, URL, email, or phone number — instantly, in your browser, with no signup required. A QR (Quick Response) code is a two-dimensional barcode readable by any smartphone camera. Originally invented for automotive manufacturing, QR codes are now used everywhere: restaurant menus, business cards, payment apps, marketing campaigns, and more.
steps: Type or paste the text, URL, phone number, or any data you want to encode.
Choose your preferred QR code size: small (128px), medium (256px), or large (512px).
Optionally pick custom foreground and background colors to match your brand.
Click Generate, then download the QR code as a PNG or copy it to your clipboard.

faq.q: What types of data can a QR code store?
faq.a: QR codes can store URLs, plain text, email addresses, phone numbers, SMS messages, Wi-Fi credentials, vCard contact info, and more. The maximum capacity is roughly 4,296 alphanumeric characters.

faq.q: Is there a size limit for QR code data?
faq.a: A single QR code can hold up to about 3 KB of data. For longer content, encode a short URL pointing to the full page rather than embedding the text directly.

faq.q: Will custom colors affect scannability?
faq.a: Yes — always ensure strong contrast between the foreground and background. Light foreground colors or similar foreground/background pairs can make the code unreadable by scanners.

faq.q: Are these QR codes free to use commercially?
faq.a: Absolutely. All QR codes generated here are completely free with no attribution required, for both personal and commercial use.

faq.q: How do I create a QR code for a website URL?
faq.a: Simply paste your full URL (e.g. https://example.com) into the input field, choose a size, and click Generate. The QR code will encode your URL so anyone who scans it is taken directly to your website.

json_formatter.name: JSON Formatter & Validator
json_formatter.description: Format, beautify, minify and validate JSON instantly in your browser. Free, private, no signup — paste your data and get a clean, readable structure in one click.
json_formatter.tagline: Paste messy JSON, get clean, readable, valid JSON back — instantly.

seo.intro:
The ManyUtils JSON Formatter is a free online tool that turns raw, minified, or broken JSON into clean, indented, human-readable text — and tells you exactly where the syntax errors are if it can't. Everything happens locally in your browser using the native JSON.parse engine, so your data is never uploaded, logged, or stored on a server.

JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is the de-facto data exchange format on the modern web. Almost every REST API, log file, configuration file, browser storage entry, and webhook payload you encounter as a developer is JSON. But JSON is also notoriously unforgiving: a single trailing comma, an unquoted key, or a stray smart quote can break your parser and crash your build. This formatter is built for those moments — when you've copied a payload from a network tab, a Slack message, or a Stack Overflow answer, and you need to see the structure clearly and confirm it's valid before pasting it into your code.

Use it to format API responses, debug production logs, prepare fixtures for tests, prettify configuration files, validate webhook payloads, or simply learn how a piece of data is structured. It supports 2-space, 4-space, and tab indentation, one-click minification for production, and a strict validator that reports the exact line and column of any syntax error.

valueProps.title: 100% browser-based — privacy by default
valueProps.body: Your JSON never leaves your device. There's no upload, no server round trip, and no log. Safe for API keys, customer records, and proprietary payloads.

valueProps.title: Instant feedback, even on large payloads
valueProps.body: Format, validate, and minify run synchronously in the browser. Most real-world payloads (API responses, log lines, configs) are processed in under a millisecond.

valueProps.title: Clear, actionable error messages
valueProps.body: If your JSON is invalid, the validator points to the exact position of the problem — not a generic 'Unexpected token' wall of red.

valueProps.title: Works offline once loaded
valueProps.body: After the page loads, the formatter keeps working without an internet connection. Useful on planes, in restricted networks, or on locked-down corporate machines.

valueProps.title: Three indentation styles
valueProps.body: Match your team's style guide: 2 spaces (most JS / TS projects), 4 spaces (Python-style), or tabs (Go and many config files).

valueProps.title: No signup, no ads on the editor itself
valueProps.body: The tool UI stays clean. Ads only appear in clearly-labelled spots around the article content, never inside or above the editor.

steps: Paste your raw or minified JSON into the Input JSON textarea. You can paste copy/pasted API responses, log entries, or content from a file.
Pick your preferred indentation — 2 spaces, 4 spaces, or tabs — from the Indent dropdown.
Click Format / Beautify to pretty-print the JSON with proper indentation and line breaks. The output appears below the buttons.
Click Minify to remove every byte of unnecessary whitespace and produce a single-line string ready for transport or storage.
Click Validate to check syntax without changing the layout. If something is wrong you'll get a clear error message with the position of the problem.
Click Copy on the output panel to copy the result to your clipboard with one click.

examples.title: Minify before sending over the wire
Catch an invalid JSON payload
examples.output: Error: Unexpected token } in JSON at position 28 — trailing comma after "age": 30 is not valid JSON. Remove the comma to make the payload parseable.

mistakes: Trailing commas. JSON does not allow a comma after the last element of an array or object. {"a":1,} is valid JavaScript but invalid JSON.
Single quotes around keys or strings. JSON requires double quotes. {'name':'Alex'} will fail; use {"name":"Alex"}.
Unquoted keys. Even if a key looks like a valid identifier, it must be wrapped in double quotes. {name:"Alex"} is invalid JSON.
Comments inside the payload. JSON has no support for // or /* */ comments. Use a separate documentation file or switch to JSON5 / JSONC if you really need them.
NaN, Infinity, undefined. These JavaScript values are not valid JSON. Convert to null or a string before serialising.
Smart quotes from rich-text editors. Pasting from Word, Notion, or Slack can replace straight " with curly “ ” quotes that look identical but break the parser.
Mixing tabs and spaces in nested structures. JSON itself doesn't care about whitespace, but inconsistent indentation makes diffs noisy. Pick one style per file and stick to it.

Sending a JavaScript object literal instead of JSON. If you accidentally console.log an object and copy it from the console, the output is a JS literal — single quotes, unquoted keys, and all. Always copy from the network tab's Response view instead.

faq.q: What is the difference between formatting, beautifying, and pretty-printing JSON?
faq.a: They all mean the same thing: adding consistent indentation and line breaks so a human can read the structure at a glance. The values themselves are not changed — only the layout. The terms are used interchangeably across editors, libraries, and documentation.

faq.q: Is my JSON sent to your servers when I use this tool?
faq.a: No. The formatter is a client-side JavaScript page. When you click Format, Minify, or Validate, the work runs entirely inside your browser tab. We don't have a backend that processes user JSON, and we don't log the content of what you paste.

faq.q: How do I fix a JSON syntax error?
faq.a: Click Validate. The tool prints the parser's exact error — usually 'Unexpected token X at position Y'. Scroll to that position in your input. The four most common culprits are: a trailing comma, single quotes around keys/strings, an unquoted key, or a missing closing bracket/brace. Fix that one character and re-validate.

faq.q: Why would I minify JSON?
faq.a: Minified JSON is smaller — typically 30–60% smaller for human-readable payloads — which means faster transfers, lower mobile data costs, and less storage in caches, databases, or localStorage. Servers and APIs almost always send minified JSON in production for this reason.

faq.q: Can this tool handle very large JSON files?
faq.a: It comfortably handles payloads up to a few megabytes, which covers the vast majority of API responses and log entries. For multi-hundred-megabyte files (database dumps, big analytics exports), the synchronous browser parser becomes slow — in those cases use a streaming parser like ijson (Python) or stream-json (Node.js), or jq from the command line.

faq.q: Does the tool support JSON5, JSONC, or NDJSON?
faq.a: It supports strict, standards-compliant JSON only — the format every API and library agrees on. JSON5 (with comments and trailing commas) and NDJSON / JSON Lines (one JSON object per line) are different formats that require dedicated parsers. We may add a separate JSON5 tool in the future.

faq.q: Will this tool change the order of my keys?
faq.a: No. Both formatting and minifying preserve the original key order. JSON objects are technically unordered per the spec, but every modern parser preserves insertion order, and so does this tool.

faq.q: Can I save my formatted JSON?
faq.a: Click Copy to copy the result to your clipboard, then paste it into a file in your editor or save it from there. We deliberately don't auto-download files so the tool stays single-purpose and frictionless.

faq.q: Does the formatter work on mobile?
faq.a: Yes. The layout is mobile-first: textareas resize, buttons stack, and the output panel scrolls horizontally for long lines. You can format and validate JSON entirely from your phone — handy for debugging webhooks on the go.

faq.q: Is this tool free for commercial use?
faq.a: Yes. The tool, its UI, and the output it produces are completely free for both personal and commercial use, with no attribution required.

password_generator.name: Password Generator
password_generator.description: Create strong, secure random passwords with customizable options.

seo.intro: This strong password generator creates cryptographically secure, random passwords instantly — entirely in your browser, with nothing stored or transmitted. A strong password is your first line of defense against unauthorized account access. Use this free password generator to create unique passwords for every account: customize the length (8–128 characters), choose character sets (uppercase, lowercase, numbers, symbols), and generate up to 10 passwords at once.
steps: Drag the length slider to set the number of characters (8–128). Longer is always stronger.
Check or uncheck character sets: uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols.
Choose how many passwords to generate at once (1, 5, or 10).
Click Generate or let the tool auto-generate, then copy your password with one click.

faq.q: What makes a password strong?
faq.a: A strong password is long (16+ characters), random, and uses a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols. Avoid dictionary words, names, or predictable patterns.

faq.q: Is this tool safe to use?
faq.a: Yes. Passwords are generated entirely in your browser using the Web Crypto API (crypto.getRandomValues). Nothing is sent to a server or stored anywhere.

faq.q: Should I use a password manager?
faq.a: Yes — a password manager lets you use a unique, complex password for every account without having to memorize them. Generate a strong password here and save it in your manager.

faq.q: How often should I change my passwords?
faq.a: Security experts now recommend changing passwords only when there's a reason to suspect a breach, rather than on a fixed schedule. The most important thing is using a unique password for every site.

faq.q: What is the most secure password length?
faq.a: For most accounts, 16 characters is considered very strong. For high-value accounts (banking, email, admin panels), use 20+ characters. This generator supports lengths up to 128 characters.

uuid_generator.name: UUID Generator
uuid_generator.description: Generate unique UUIDs (v4) for your applications instantly.

seo.intro: Generate UUID v4 online instantly with this free tool — no signup, no installation required. A UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) is a 128-bit label used to uniquely identify objects in software systems. Version 4 UUIDs are randomly generated, making collisions virtually impossible. They are perfect for database primary keys, session tokens, unique resource IDs in APIs, file names, and distributed system identifiers. Use the bulk generator to produce up to 100 UUIDs at once.
steps: A single UUID v4 is generated automatically when the page loads.
Click Generate to create a new random UUID, or use the bulk generator to produce up to 100 at once.
Toggle uppercase/lowercase and with/without hyphens to match your requirements.
Click any UUID to copy it to your clipboard instantly.

faq.q: What is a UUID v4?
faq.a: UUID v4 is a randomly generated universally unique identifier. It contains 122 random bits, giving a total of 2^122 possible values — making accidental collisions practically impossible.

faq.q: When should I use UUIDs?
faq.a: Use UUIDs as primary keys in databases, unique identifiers for API resources, session tokens, file names, and anywhere you need a globally unique string that doesn't expose sequential information.

faq.q: Are UUIDs truly unique?
faq.a: While not mathematically guaranteed, the probability of two randomly generated UUIDs colliding is astronomically low — about 1 in 5.3 × 10^36. In practice, they are treated as unique.

faq.q: What is the difference between UUID v1, v4, and v7?
faq.a: v1 is time-based (may expose the machine's MAC address), v4 is fully random, and v7 (newer) combines a timestamp with randomness for sortability. v4 is the most widely used for general purposes.

faq.q: Can I generate multiple UUIDs at once?
faq.a: Yes. Enter a count between 1 and 100 in the bulk generator and click Bulk Generate. All UUIDs are displayed in a scrollable list and can be copied to your clipboard with a single click.

faq.q: Will the downloaded image match what I see in the preview?

image_compressor.name: Image Compressor
image_compressor.description: Compress and reduce image file size while maintaining quality.

seo.intro: Large images slow down websites and consume unnecessary storage. This tool compresses images directly in your browser, reducing file size by up to 80% while preserving as much visual quality as possible — no uploading to a server required.
steps: Click the upload area or drag and drop your image onto it.

faq.q: Which format should I choose for best compression?
faq.a: WebP typically achieves the best compression with excellent quality, followed by JPEG. Use PNG only when you need transparency or lossless quality, as it produces larger files.

faq.q: What quality level should I use?
faq.a: For web images, 75–85% quality is usually ideal — it produces a significant file size reduction with barely noticeable quality loss. Go lower (50–70%) for thumbnails or background images.

faq.q: Does compression reduce image dimensions?
faq.a: No, unless you explicitly set a max width or height. Compression only reduces file size. Use the resize inputs if you also want to change dimensions.

faq.q: Is my image data private?
faq.a: Yes. Images are processed entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. No data is ever uploaded to a server.

css_gradient_generator.name: CSS Gradient Generator
css_gradient_generator.description: Design beautiful CSS gradients with a visual editor and copy the code.

seo.intro: CSS gradients let you create smooth transitions between colors without using image files. This visual editor makes it easy to design linear, radial, and conic gradients with custom color stops, angles, and positions — then copy the ready-to-use CSS with one click.
steps: Choose a gradient type: linear (straight), radial (circular), or conic (angular sweep).
Adjust the angle or direction using the slider (for linear gradients).
Set your color stops — pick colors and drag the position sliders to control where each color appears.
Click Copy CSS to copy the generated code and paste it directly into your stylesheet.

faq.q: What is a CSS gradient?
faq.a: A CSS gradient is a smooth color transition defined in CSS using the `linear-gradient()`, `radial-gradient()`, or `conic-gradient()` functions. They are rendered by the browser without needing any image files.

faq.q: How many color stops can I add?
faq.a: This tool supports up to 5 color stops. In standard CSS there is no hard limit on the number of stops a gradient can have.

faq.q: What is the difference between linear and radial gradients?
faq.a: A linear gradient transitions colors along a straight line at a given angle. A radial gradient radiates outward from a central point in a circular or elliptical pattern.

faq.q: Will the generated CSS work in all browsers?
faq.a: Yes. CSS gradients are fully supported in all modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge). No vendor prefixes are needed for current browser versions.

color_palette_generator.name: Color Palette Generator
color_palette_generator.description: Generate harmonious color palettes for your design projects.

seo.intro: Good color choices are the foundation of great design. This tool generates harmonious 5-color palettes based on proven color theory rules — complementary, analogous, triadic, tetradic, and monochromatic — starting from any base color you choose.
steps: Pick a base color using the color picker, or type a hex code directly into the input.
Choose a color harmony type from the dropdown (complementary, analogous, triadic, tetradic, or monochromatic).
The palette generates instantly. Click any swatch to copy its hex code.
Click Copy CSS Variables to get all 5 colors as CSS custom properties ready to paste into your stylesheet.

faq.q: What is color harmony?
faq.a: Color harmony refers to combinations of colors that are pleasing to the eye because they follow specific relationships on the color wheel. Common harmonies include complementary (opposite colors), analogous (adjacent colors), and triadic (evenly spaced thirds).

faq.q: What is the difference between analogous and triadic palettes?
faq.a: An analogous palette uses colors that sit next to each other on the color wheel, creating a cohesive, calm look. A triadic palette uses three colors evenly spaced (120° apart), creating a more vibrant, high-contrast combination.

faq.q: What is a monochromatic palette?
faq.a: A monochromatic palette uses variations of a single hue — different lightness and saturation levels — creating a refined, elegant look that's easy to apply consistently throughout a design.

faq.q: Can I use these palettes for commercial projects?
faq.a: Yes, absolutely. Colors cannot be copyrighted. Any palette you generate here is free to use in personal or commercial projects.

base64_encoder_decoder.name: Base64 Encoder / Decoder
base64_encoder_decoder.description: Encode text to Base64 or decode Base64 strings back to text.

seo.intro: Encode text to Base64 online or decode Base64 strings back to plain text — instantly, for free, with no signup required. Base64 is an encoding scheme that converts binary or text data into a portable string of ASCII characters. It is widely used to embed images inline in HTML and CSS (data URIs), transmit binary data in JSON payloads, encode email attachments (MIME), pass data safely in URLs, and store binary data in text-based systems like databases and configuration files.
steps: Choose a mode: Encode (text → Base64) or Decode (Base64 → text).
Type or paste your input text into the left area.
The output updates automatically, or click the Encode/Decode button.
Click Copy to copy the output, or use the Swap button to flip input and output.

faq.q: What is Base64 encoding?
faq.a: Base64 converts data into a string using 64 safe ASCII characters (A–Z, a–z, 0–9, +, /). It increases data size by about 33% but makes binary data safe to transmit in text-based protocols.

faq.q: Is Base64 encryption?
faq.a: No. Base64 is an encoding scheme, not encryption. It does not provide any security. Anyone can decode a Base64 string without a key. Never use Base64 to hide sensitive data.

faq.q: Why does Base64 output end with = or ==?
faq.a: The = characters are padding. Base64 encodes data in 3-byte chunks. If the input length isn't a multiple of 3, padding characters are added to ensure the output length is a multiple of 4.

faq.q: What is URL-safe Base64?
faq.a: Standard Base64 uses + and / which have special meanings in URLs. URL-safe Base64 replaces these with - and _ so the encoded string can be safely used in URLs and filenames.

faq.q: How do I encode an image to Base64?
faq.a: To encode a binary file (like an image) to Base64, you would need to read the file as binary data first. This tool handles text-to-Base64 encoding. For binary files, use a file-upload Base64 tool or a command like: base64 -i image.png on macOS/Linux.

currency_converter.name: Currency Converter
currency_converter.description: Convert between world currencies using the latest exchange rates.

seo.intro: This currency converter supports 32 major world currencies and fetches live exchange rates when available. All conversions happen instantly in your browser — no account or API key needed.
steps: Enter the amount you want to convert in the amount field.
Select the source currency (From) and the target currency (To) from the dropdowns.
The result updates automatically as you type or change currencies.
Use the Swap button to reverse the conversion direction, or click a quick-pair button for common conversions.

faq.q: How accurate are the exchange rates?
faq.a: The tool attempts to fetch live rates from a free exchange rate API. If the request fails (e.g. due to network issues), it falls back to periodically updated hardcoded rates. Live rates should be accurate to within a few minutes.

faq.q: Why does it say 'approximate'?
faq.a: When live rate fetching fails, the tool uses built-in fallback rates that may be slightly out of date. For financial transactions, always verify rates with your bank or a financial institution.

faq.q: Which currencies are supported?
faq.a: The tool supports 32 major currencies including USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD, CHF, CNY, INR, BRL, MXN, KRW, and more. New currencies may be added in future updates.

faq.q: Can I use this for financial transactions?
faq.a: This tool is intended for informational and planning purposes only. For actual financial transactions, use rates provided by your bank, broker, or official financial service.

word_character_counter.name: Word & Character Counter
word_character_counter.description: Count words, characters, sentences, and paragraphs in your text.

seo.intro: Whether you're writing an essay, a tweet, a meta description, or an article, keeping track of your word and character count is essential. This tool provides real-time statistics as you type, including reading time and speaking time estimates.
steps: Type or paste your text into the large textarea.
Statistics update live — no button click needed.
Review the stat cards: characters (with/without spaces), words, sentences, paragraphs, and average word length.
Check the estimated reading time and speaking time at the bottom of the stats.

faq.q: How is reading time calculated?
faq.a: Reading time is estimated at 200 words per minute, which is the average adult silent reading speed. The displayed time is rounded to the nearest practical unit (seconds, minutes, or hours).

faq.q: How is speaking time calculated?
faq.a: Speaking time is estimated at 150 words per minute, the average for a comfortable presentation pace. This is useful for estimating speech or podcast length.

faq.q: How are sentences counted?
faq.a: Sentences are counted by splitting the text on sentence-ending punctuation (., !, ?). This is a heuristic and may not be perfectly accurate for texts that use punctuation in unusual ways.

faq.q: What counts as a word?
faq.a: Words are counted by splitting on whitespace and filtering out empty strings. Any sequence of non-whitespace characters is treated as a word, including numbers and hyphenated words.

days_between_dates.name: Days Between Dates
days_between_dates.description: Calculate the number of days, weeks, and months between two dates.

seo.intro: Need to know how many days until a deadline, how long ago an event occurred, or how many business days are in a period? This date calculator gives you a complete breakdown including total days, weeks, business days, and hours.

The result updates automatically. Review the breakdown: total days, weeks, months, business days, and hours.
Use the Swap button to reverse start and end dates, or the Today shortcut to reset either date to today.

faq.q: How are business days calculated?
faq.a: Business days exclude Saturdays and Sundays. Public holidays are not automatically excluded since they vary by country and region. You can manually adjust for holidays.

faq.q: What if the end date is before the start date?

faq.q: How accurate is the month calculation?
faq.a: The month figure is an approximation (total days ÷ 30.44). For exact calendar months between two dates, note that months have different lengths, so this is always an estimate.

faq.q: Can I calculate dates in the past?
faq.a: Yes. You can enter any two dates — past, present, or future — and the calculator will show the difference. A status badge indicates whether the end date is in the past or future.

png_to_jpg.name: PNG to JPG Converter
png_to_jpg.description: Convert PNG images to JPG (JPEG) directly in your browser — fast, free, no upload.

seo.intro: PNG and JPG are the two most common image formats on the web — but they're built for different jobs. PNG keeps every pixel exactly as it was saved, including transparency, which makes file sizes large. JPG (also called JPEG) uses lossy compression that throws away tiny details your eye can't easily see, producing files that are 5–10× smaller. If you have a PNG screenshot, photo or graphic that doesn't need transparency, converting it to JPG is the fastest way to make it lighter for email, web pages, or storage. This converter runs entirely in your browser — your image never gets uploaded.
steps: Drop or pick your PNG — Drag a PNG into the upload box, or click to browse. Files of any size are supported as long as your browser can hold them in memory.
Choose your quality — Move the quality slider. 90% is a great default — visually lossless for most images. Drop to 75% for very small files.
Download the JPG — Click Download. The JPG saves to your device with the same base filename and a .jpg extension.

faq.q: Will my PNG transparency be preserved?
faq.a: No. JPG does not support transparency. Any transparent areas in your PNG will be filled with white. If you need transparency, use our JPG to PNG or PNG to WebP converter instead.

faq.q: How small will the JPG be?
faq.a: Typically 5–15× smaller than the source PNG, depending on the image content. Photos compress dramatically; flat-colour graphics less so.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. The conversion happens entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. We never see your image.

faq.q: Is there a file size limit?
faq.a: No hard limit. The only constraint is your browser's memory. Most modern browsers comfortably handle 50 MB+ images.

faq.q: What quality should I pick?
faq.a: For most uses, 85–90% is indistinguishable from the original to the human eye and produces tiny files. Go below 75% only when bytes matter more than visual fidelity.

jpg_to_png.name: JPG to PNG Converter
jpg_to_png.description: Convert JPG (JPEG) images to lossless PNG in your browser — keep transparency support.

seo.intro: Converting JPG to PNG is most useful when you need to add transparency, edit the image without re-introducing JPEG artifacts, or feed the image into a tool that requires PNG. Note that JPG is lossy — once compression has been applied, the data is gone. Converting to PNG won't magically restore detail, but it will stop *further* loss from happening on subsequent saves. Common use cases: preparing images for vector editing, removing backgrounds in another tool, or supplying assets to systems that mandate PNG.
steps: Upload your JPG — Drag a JPG/JPEG into the drop zone, or click to browse.
Convert — PNG is lossless, so there's no quality slider. Click Convert.
Download — A .png file with identical pixels (no further loss) is generated and ready to download.

faq.q: Does the PNG add transparency to my JPG?
faq.a: No. JPG cannot store transparency, so we cannot invent it. Convert to PNG first, then use a background-removal tool to add transparency.

faq.q: Will the PNG be larger than the JPG?
faq.a: Usually yes — often 3–5× larger. PNG is lossless and JPG is lossy, so this is unavoidable. Use PNG when quality matters more than size.

faq.q: Is anything uploaded?
faq.a: No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser. Your file never leaves your device.

png_to_webp.name: PNG to WebP Converter
png_to_webp.description: Convert PNG to WebP — modern format with up to 30 % smaller files at the same quality.

seo.intro: WebP is Google's modern image format that offers both lossless and lossy compression, with file sizes typically 25–35% smaller than equivalent PNG/JPG at the same quality. WebP supports transparency *and* animation, making it a near-universal replacement. All modern browsers — Chrome, Firefox, Safari (since 14), Edge — display WebP natively. Converting your PNG to WebP is one of the highest-leverage things you can do for site speed.
steps: Drop your PNG — Pick the PNG you want to convert.
Adjust quality — WebP at quality 80 looks identical to PNG for most images and is ~70% smaller. Crank up for art and screenshots.
Download — Save the .webp file. It's ready to ship to a CDN or attach to email.

faq.q: Is WebP supported everywhere?
faq.a: All major modern browsers support WebP. Older Safari (≤13), some legacy email clients and a few image viewers do not. For maximum compatibility, also keep a JPG fallback.

faq.q: Does WebP keep transparency?
faq.a: Yes. Unlike JPG, WebP preserves alpha channels, so transparent PNGs convert cleanly.

faq.q: How much smaller will the WebP be?
faq.a: Typically 25–35% smaller than the PNG. Photographic content compresses more than flat graphics.

webp_to_png.name: WebP to PNG Converter
webp_to_png.description: Convert WebP images to lossless PNG — works on any browser, no upload.

seo.intro: Some applications, image editors, and older systems still expect PNG. If you've received a WebP file from a website or modern app and need to use it somewhere that doesn't accept WebP yet (think: certain CMS uploaders, legacy email clients, ancient print pipelines), converting to PNG is the safest choice — PNG is universally supported and lossless.
steps: Upload your WebP — Drag a .webp file into the drop zone, or click to pick one.
Convert — PNG is lossless — there's no quality slider. The convert button creates an identical-looking PNG.
Download — Save the .png file. Transparency, if present, is preserved.

faq.q: Is transparency preserved?
faq.a: Yes. PNG fully supports the alpha channel that WebP uses, so transparent areas stay transparent.

faq.q: Why is the PNG bigger than the WebP?
faq.a: PNG is lossless and uses an older compression scheme. Most converted PNGs end up 2–4× larger than the source WebP — that's expected.

faq.q: Does this work with animated WebP?
faq.a: No. Browser canvas APIs only render the first frame, so animations are flattened. Use a dedicated WebP-to-GIF tool for animations.

webp_to_jpg.name: WebP to JPG Converter
webp_to_jpg.description: Convert WebP images to widely-compatible JPG — useful for older email clients and apps.

seo.intro: JPG is still the broadest-compatibility raster format on the planet — every email client, every print shop, every cheap image viewer reads it. If you need to share a WebP image with someone whose tools don't recognise the format, converting to JPG is the reliable answer. Note that JPG is lossy and cannot represent transparency: any transparent areas in your WebP will be filled with white in the converted JPG.
steps: Drop your WebP — Drag the .webp file in, or click to browse.
Pick your quality — For email and casual sharing, 85% is a great balance. Drop to 70% for tiny attachments.
Download — A .jpg ready for any platform — email, social, CMS, print.

faq.q: Will transparent areas be preserved?
faq.a: No. JPG can't store transparency. Transparent pixels will be filled with white. If you need transparency, convert to PNG instead.

faq.q: Can I convert animated WebPs to animated JPGs?
faq.a: JPG isn't an animated format. Use our WebP to GIF or video-to-GIF tool if you need animation.

jpg_to_webp.name: JPG to WebP Converter
jpg_to_webp.description: Convert JPG to WebP for smaller, web-optimised images — great for blogs and product pages.

seo.intro: Replacing JPG with WebP on a website typically cuts image bytes by 25–35% with no perceptible quality loss — that's a giant Lighthouse / Core Web Vitals win for very little effort. Use this tool whenever you have a JPG asset destined for the web (blog post images, e-commerce product shots, OG images) and the audience is on modern browsers.
steps: Drop your JPG — Drag a JPG into the upload box, or click to browse.
Pick a quality — WebP at quality 80 looks visually identical for most photos and is roughly 30% smaller than the source JPG.
Download the WebP — The new .webp file is ready for your CDN or product page.

faq.q: Will the WebP look worse than the JPG?
faq.a: At quality 80+, no. WebP often retains slightly more detail than JPG at the same file size, especially in flat colour areas.

faq.q: How does it affect SEO and Core Web Vitals?
faq.a: Switching to WebP usually improves the LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) metric and overall page weight, which Google uses as a ranking signal.

svg_to_png.name: SVG to PNG Converter
svg_to_png.description: Rasterise SVG to high-quality PNG at any size — preserves transparency.

seo.intro: SVG is great for scalable graphics, but a lot of contexts still expect raster images: social-media uploaders, certain CMSes, design boards, presentations, photo printers. This tool rasterises your SVG to a high-quality PNG using the browser's SVG renderer, so the result is pixel-perfect at the chosen size.
steps: Drop your SVG — Drag an .svg file into the upload area, or click to pick one.
Convert — The SVG is rendered onto a canvas at its intrinsic dimensions and saved as PNG.
Download — Save the .png. Transparency is preserved.

faq.q: Why does my PNG look fuzzy?
faq.a: Most likely your SVG didn't declare a width/height. We render at 1024×1024 by default in that case. Add explicit width="..." height="..." to your SVG, or use the resizer afterwards.

faq.q: Are external assets (fonts, images) loaded?
faq.a: External fonts loaded with @font-face from another origin may not render due to browser security. Embed fonts with data URIs or convert text to paths.

faq.q: Is anything uploaded?
faq.a: No. SVG is rendered entirely in your browser using the Canvas API.

svg_to_jpg.name: SVG to JPG Converter
svg_to_jpg.description: Rasterise SVG to JPG with a chosen background colour — perfect for thumbnails and emails.

seo.intro: When you need a JPG version of an SVG — for an email signature, a thumbnail in a system that requires JPG, or sharing a graphic with someone whose tools don't support SVG — this tool rasterises the SVG and fills the background with white (since JPG can't carry transparency).
steps: Drop your SVG — Drag your .svg into the upload box.
Pick your quality — 90% is a great default for graphics with sharp edges; drop to 75% only for visual content where size matters.
Download — A .jpg with a white background is generated.

faq.q: Why is the background white?
faq.a: JPG cannot store transparency, so we fill transparent areas with white. If you need transparency, use SVG to PNG instead.

faq.q: Can I get a different background colour?
faq.a: Currently only white. For custom backgrounds, convert to PNG first then use an editor to set the background.

svg_to_webp.name: SVG to WebP Converter
svg_to_webp.description: Rasterise SVG to WebP for compact, modern raster images.

seo.intro: WebP is a modern raster format with broad browser support and much smaller files than PNG. Converting SVG to WebP gives you a compact raster suitable for OG images, blog headers, and shipped product assets, while keeping transparency intact.
steps: Upload your SVG — Drag the .svg in, or click to pick.
Pick your quality — Quality 80 is a strong default — small files, no visible loss for most graphics.
Download — Save the .webp. Transparency is preserved.

faq.q: Will transparency be preserved?
faq.a: Yes. WebP supports the same alpha channel as PNG, so transparent SVG areas remain transparent.

faq.q: Why use WebP over PNG for SVG output?
faq.a: WebP files are typically 25–40% smaller than PNG at the same visual quality, which makes a big difference for web performance.

image_resizer.name: Image Resizer
image_resizer.description: Resize images by exact pixel dimensions or percentage with optional aspect-ratio lock.

seo.intro: Resizing images is one of the most-asked-for image operations on the web — for profile pictures with a strict pixel limit, blog images that need to fit a layout, social media thumbnails, or shrinking photos before email. Our resizer lets you specify exact pixel dimensions, percentage scaling, and choose any common output format. It runs entirely in your browser using the Canvas API, so your photos never leave your device.
steps: Upload your image — Drag any PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF into the drop zone, or click to browse.
Set your dimensions — Type a target width or height, or use percent. Keep "Aspect ratio" on to scale proportionally.
Pick output format and quality — WebP for the smallest size, PNG for transparency, JPG for max compatibility.
Download — Click Download to save the resized image.

faq.q: Will my image get blurry?
faq.a: Scaling down (e.g. 4000 × 3000 → 800 × 600) is essentially lossless. Scaling up adds blur — there's no detail to invent. Always start from the largest source you have.

faq.q: How do I resize for a specific use case (e.g. Twitter, Instagram)?
faq.a: Common targets: Instagram square 1080 × 1080, Twitter post 1200 × 675, Open Graph 1200 × 630, favicon 192 × 192.

faq.q: Is anything uploaded?
faq.a: No. Everything runs in your browser; we never see your file.

crop_image.name: Crop Image
crop_image.description: Crop images with drag-to-select, ratio presets (1:1, 4:3, 16:9), or pixel-precise inputs.

seo.intro: Cropping is a precision operation — pixels matter. Our cropper lets you drag a selection rectangle directly on the image, snap to common ratios (square, 4:3, 16:9, 9:16) for social media presets, or type exact x/y/width/height coordinates when you need pixel-perfect output. The full-resolution source is preserved at all times — the on-screen preview is just scaled to fit your viewport.
steps: Upload your image — Drop a PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF.
Set your crop area — Drag a new selection on the image, or grab the corner handles to resize.
Pick a ratio (optional) — Click 1:1 for square, 16:9 for landscape, 9:16 for vertical stories — the selection auto-locks.
Apply and download — Click Apply Crop, then Download.

faq.q: Are pixels lost when cropping?
faq.a: Only the pixels outside the crop rectangle are discarded. The kept area retains its full resolution.

faq.q: Can I crop multiple images at once?
faq.a: Currently this tool processes one image at a time. We may add a batch mode in the future — let us know if you need it.

faq.q: Does it work on touch screens?
faq.a: Yes. The selection box uses pointer events, so touch and mouse work the same way.

rotate_flip_image.name: Rotate & Flip Image
rotate_flip_image.description: Rotate by 90°, 180°, 270° or any custom angle and flip horizontally or vertically.

seo.intro: Sometimes a photo comes out sideways from your phone, a screenshot needs flipping for a tutorial, or a graphic needs mirroring for a layout. This tool rotates by 90° increments or any custom angle (with the canvas auto-resized so nothing is clipped) and flips horizontally or vertically. Everything happens in your browser.
steps: Drop an image — Drag any PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF.
Use the action buttons — Rotate 90° / -90° / 180°, flip horizontal, flip vertical. Or type a custom angle.
Pick a format — Output as PNG (preserves transparency), JPG, or WebP.
Download — Click Download to save the result.

faq.q: Why does the canvas grow when I rotate?
faq.a: Diagonal rotations need a larger bounding box to avoid clipping the corners. We auto-resize the canvas so the entire rotated image fits.

faq.q: Will it correct EXIF orientation automatically?
faq.a: Modern browsers honour EXIF orientation when decoding, so the tool sees the visually-correct image. Manual rotation lets you go further.

video_to_gif.name: Video to GIF Converter
video_to_gif.description: Turn short videos (≤ 30s, ≤ 100 MB) into optimised animated GIFs entirely in your browser.

seo.intro: Animated GIFs are still everywhere — slack, GitHub, Twitter, blog posts. Converting a short video clip to a GIF used to mean uploading to a sketchy site. This tool runs the entire conversion in your browser: we extract frames using the browser's video decoder and encode them with the GIF encoder library lazy-loaded only when you click Convert. Your file never leaves your device.
steps: Upload a video — Drop an MP4, MOV, WebM or other browser-supported video. Max 100 MB and 30 seconds.
Trim and tune — Set start/end seconds, pick FPS (12 is a great default), and choose an output width (480 px is a balanced choice).
Convert — Click Convert to GIF. The encoder loads (~30 KB) and processing happens locally with a progress bar.
Download — Save the .gif file. Smaller clips and lower FPS give smaller files.

faq.q: Why is there a 30-second limit?
faq.a: GIF is an inefficient format. A 30-second 480p clip at 12 FPS is already 5–10 MB. Anything longer becomes impractical.

faq.q: Is my video uploaded?
faq.a: No. Everything happens in your browser — frame extraction and GIF encoding both run locally.

faq.q: How can I make smaller GIFs?
faq.a: Reduce FPS (12 → 8), shrink the width (480 → 320), and trim aggressively. Each cuts size roughly proportionally.

faq.q: Why does conversion feel slow on my phone?
faq.a: GIF encoding is CPU-intensive. Trimming the clip to a few seconds and dropping FPS dramatically speeds things up.

audio_cutter.name: Audio Cutter
audio_cutter.description: Trim and cut MP3, WAV, M4A and other audio files with sub-second precision in your browser.

seo.intro: Audio cutting is one of the most common tasks anyone working with sound runs into — trimming silence at the start of a podcast, isolating a quote from a long recording, removing the awkward few seconds at the end of a voicemail. Our audio cutter uses the Web Audio API to decode any browser-supported format (MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, OGG, FLAC) and writes a precise, lossless WAV cut entirely in your browser.
steps: Drop an audio file — Drag any MP3 / WAV / M4A / AAC / OGG / FLAC into the upload area.
Pick start and end times — Use the range sliders or type exact seconds — sub-second precision.
Cut and preview — Click Cut & preview to hear the result before downloading.
Download — Save the cut as a 16-bit PCM WAV file.

faq.q: Why is the output a WAV file even if I uploaded an MP3?
faq.a: MP3 encoding in the browser without a heavy library (LAME) isn't practical. WAV is universally supported and lossless. You can re-encode to MP3 with our future MP3 encoder, or use a desktop tool.

faq.q: Does it preserve audio quality?
faq.a: Yes. Decoding to PCM and re-encoding as WAV is lossless — you only lose information when you re-encode to a lossy format like MP3 / AAC.

faq.q: What's the maximum file size?
faq.a: Limited only by your browser's memory. Most modern browsers handle 200 MB+ comfortably.

volume_changer.name: Audio Volume Booster & Reducer
volume_changer.description: Boost quiet audio or reduce loud audio from -20 dB to +20 dB. 100 % browser-based.

seo.intro: Voice notes that sound great on your phone but tinny on someone else's laptop, podcasts that vary in level between guests, lectures recorded too quietly — all common problems. The volume changer applies a constant gain (in decibels) to every sample of your audio file, in your browser. ±20 dB is the practical limit before clipping becomes audible.
steps: Upload audio — Drop an MP3, WAV, M4A or other audio file.
Set the gain — +6 dB is "noticeably louder", +10 dB is "much louder". -6 dB roughly halves the volume. Try small steps first.
Apply and preview — Listen to the result before downloading.
Download — Save the boosted/reduced version as a WAV.

faq.q: Will boosting too much distort my audio?
faq.a: Yes. Going beyond about +12 dB on already-loud audio causes clipping (hard distortion). Start small.

faq.q: Can I normalise to a specific peak level?
faq.a: This tool applies a constant gain. For peak/LUFS normalisation, use a desktop DAW.

audio_speed_changer.name: Audio Speed Changer
audio_speed_changer.description: Speed audio up to 4× or slow down to 0.25× — useful for podcasts and language practice.

seo.intro: Speeding up podcasts to fit them in a commute, slowing down a song to learn a riff on guitar, or making a lecture digestible — speed changing is one of the most useful audio tools for everyday use. This tool uses linear interpolation to resample your audio. As is standard for "speed change without preserving pitch", faster playback raises the pitch and slower playback lowers it, which is what most users actually want.
steps: Upload audio — Drop any browser-supported audio file.
Pick a speed — Use the slider or one of the presets. 1.5× and 2× are great for podcasts; 0.5× for music transcription.
Apply and preview — Hear the result before saving.
Download — Save the time-stretched WAV file.

faq.q: Why does the pitch change?
faq.a: Resampling without time-stretching changes pitch with speed. Pitch-preserving time-stretch (PSOLA, phase vocoder) needs a much heavier algorithm and is on our roadmap.

faq.q: Is there a quality loss?
faq.a: Linear interpolation introduces a tiny amount of high-frequency softening. For voice content it's inaudible; for high-quality music, use a DAW.

audio_to_wav.name: Audio to WAV Converter
audio_to_wav.description: Convert MP3, M4A, AAC, OGG, FLAC and more into uncompressed 16-bit PCM WAV files.

seo.intro: WAV is the universal "raw PCM" container — every operating system, every audio editor, every embedded device understands it. Converting MP3, M4A, AAC, OGG or FLAC to WAV is useful when you need to feed audio into a tool that doesn't accept compressed formats, or when you want a lossless working copy before further editing. The browser's Web Audio API decodes the source and we write a 16-bit stereo (or mono) WAV file using the same parameters as the input.
steps: Upload audio — Drop any browser-decodable audio file.
Convert — Click Convert to WAV. Decoding + re-encoding usually takes <2 seconds for a 5-minute file.
Download — Save the .wav.

faq.q: Will the WAV be much larger than my MP3?
faq.a: Typically 5–10× larger. WAV is uncompressed — that's the trade-off for universal compatibility and zero generational loss.

faq.q: Does it support every audio format?
faq.a: It supports every format your browser can decode via the Web Audio API: MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, OGG (Vorbis), FLAC. Browser support varies slightly — Safari may struggle with Ogg Vorbis on older versions.

mp3_metadata_viewer.name: MP3 Metadata Viewer
mp3_metadata_viewer.description: View ID3v1 and ID3v2 tags inside MP3 files: title, artist, album, year, genre, embedded artwork.

seo.intro: Every MP3 file has metadata baked into it — the title, artist, album, year, genre, comment, and often an embedded album cover. This is the data your music player uses to show "Now playing" cards. Sometimes you want to see what's in there: when troubleshooting a misnamed track, when an MP3 export from a recorder shows weird tags, or just out of curiosity. This viewer reads ID3v1 (legacy 128-byte footer) and ID3v2 (modern, prepended) tags, including embedded artwork, all in your browser.
steps: Drop an MP3 — Drag an .mp3 file into the upload area.
Read the tags — Title, artist, album, year, genre, comment and embedded artwork all appear instantly.
Reset to view another file — Click Reset to load a different MP3.

faq.q: Can I edit the tags here?
faq.a: Not yet — this tool is read-only. We're considering adding a tag editor — let us know via the contact form if you'd use one.

faq.q: What if my MP3 has no tags?
faq.a: You'll see "No tags found". Many transcoders strip tags by default — re-tag with a desktop tool like Mp3tag.

faq.q: Is the file uploaded?
faq.a: No. The file is read locally in your browser. Nothing is sent over the network.

why.title: Why ManyUtils exists
why.body: We got tired of the same online-tools experience: pop-ups, broken paywalls, ads stacked above the input box, and tools that quietly upload your private data to a server you've never heard of. ManyUtils is the opposite. Every utility on this site is free, runs entirely in your browser, loads in under a second on a basic mobile connection, and does one thing well. No account, no upload, no surprise paywall on the third use.
why.card1_body: Your inputs never leave your device. No upload, no log, no analytics on what you paste.
why.card2_body: Static HTML, vanilla JavaScript, mobile-first layout. The page is interactive before most sites have started loading.
why.card3_body: No signup, no email gate, no "create an account to copy your result". Open, use, leave.
why.card4_body: Every tool ships with a real article — examples, common mistakes, and FAQs written by people who use it daily.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: Yes. Every tool on ManyUtils is free to use without an account. The site is supported by ads displayed around the article content, never inside the tool UI itself.
faq.q2: Do you upload my data when I use a tool?
faq.a2: No. Almost all of our tools — JSON formatter, password generator, image compressor, base64 encoder, and so on — process your input entirely inside your browser. Nothing is uploaded to our servers.
faq.q3: Do I need to create an account?
faq.a3: No. ManyUtils has no login system. Every feature is fully usable on your first visit and forever after.
faq.q4: Can I use the tools on mobile?
faq.a4: Yes. Every tool is designed mobile-first: layouts, buttons, and outputs scale to small screens. You can format JSON, generate passwords, or compress an image entirely from your phone.
faq.q5: Are the outputs free for commercial use?
faq.a5: Yes. Whatever the tools produce — formatted JSON, generated passwords, color palettes, QR codes, compressed images, gradients, etc. — is yours to use for personal or commercial projects, with no attribution required.
faq.q6_html: Why are some tools missing features I'd expect?
faq.a6_html: We deliberately keep each tool focused on the most common 90% of use cases so the interface stays fast and clean. If something you need is missing, contact us — we read every request.

about.page_title: About ManyUtils — Free Online Tools for Developers & Designers
about.page_meta: ManyUtils builds fast, free, privacy-friendly online tools for developers, designers and everyday users. Learn who we are, what we believe, and how every tool is built.
about.subtitle: Free, fast, privacy-friendly online tools — built by people who got tired of opening five tabs to format a JSON file.
about.s1_body_html:
ManyUtils is an independent project that builds and maintains a growing library of free online utilities. We started in 2024 because we kept reaching for the same handful of tools — JSON formatters, password generators, image compressors — and being met with cluttered websites full of pop-ups, broken paywalls, and tools that secretly uploaded private data to a server.

So we built our own. Every tool on ManyUtils is designed around three rules: it must work in the browser without sending your data anywhere, it must load in under a second on a basic mobile connection, and it must do one thing well.
about.s2_body_html:
• Your data is yours. Tools that process your input — JSON, passwords, images, text — should never need to upload it. Almost everything we build runs entirely on your device.
  • Speed is a feature. A "free online tool" that takes ten seconds to load isn't free; it costs you attention. We aim for sub-second time-to-interactive on every page.
  • No fake walls. No "sign up to copy your result", no "upgrade to remove the watermark". Every feature you see is fully usable, forever, for free.
  • Honest content. Our articles around each tool are written by people who actually use them. Examples are tested. Mistakes are real ones we've made.
  • Ads, not surveillance. ManyUtils is supported by Google AdSense, shown in clearly labelled spots around the article — never inside or above the tool itself.
about.s3_body_html:
Every tool follows the same pattern: a static HTML page, a small piece of vanilla JavaScript, and zero server-side processing of user data. There is no account system, no database of user inputs, no tracking script that follows you around the internet. The only third-party services we use are listed transparently in our Privacy Policy.

The codebase is organised so that each tool is a self-contained page. That keeps the surface area small, the security story simple, and the load time fast — even if you only need one tool, you only download the code for that tool.
about.s4_body_html: Most of our visitors are developers and designers — people who want to format a JSON payload, generate a UUID, build a CSS gradient, or compress a screenshot before pasting it into a ticket. But we deliberately also build tools for everyday users: a strong password generator, a QR code generator, a days-between-dates calculator, a currency converter. Anyone with a browser should be able to land on ManyUtils and finish their task in under a minute.
about.s5_body_html:
Found a bug, want a new tool, or noticed a typo? We read every message.

Contact us →

contact.page_title: Contact ManyUtils — Feedback, Bug Reports & Tool Requests
contact.page_meta: Get in touch with the ManyUtils team. Report a bug, request a new tool, ask about advertising, or just say hi. We read every message.
contact.subtitle: We're a small team. We read everything you send us, and we usually reply within two business days.
contact.email_body: For all enquiries — bug reports, feature requests, advertising, partnerships, press, or general feedback — send an email to:
contact.include_intro: To help us reply faster, please include:
contact.card_bug_body: The tool URL, what you tried to do, what happened, what you expected, and (if you can) your browser and OS version.
contact.card_feature_body: A short description of the use case. Real workflows beat abstract feature lists every time.
contact.card_ads_body: Your company, what you'd like to promote, and your monthly budget range.
contact.card_press_body: Outlet, deadline, and a few sample questions or topics.
contact.faq_q1: Do you offer paid support or custom tools?
contact.faq_a1: For custom internal tools, white-label utilities, or sponsored tools, email us at the address above with the brief.
contact.faq_q2: Can I use ManyUtils tools on my own site?
contact.faq_a2: The output of any tool (formatted JSON, generated passwords, gradients, palettes, QR codes, etc.) is yours to use freely, including commercially. Embedding the tools themselves into your own site is not currently supported — please get in touch if that's something you need.
contact.faq_q3: How do I report a privacy or security issue?
contact.faq_a3: Please email us with "Security" in the subject line. We treat security reports with the highest priority.
contact.faq_q4: Do you reply in languages other than English?
contact.faq_a4: Yes — feel free to write in English, French, Spanish, German or Portuguese. We'll reply in the same language.
